title: West Pikeland votes to sell SALT Performing Arts' home, leaving the theater's future open
summary: Township supervisors voted 3-2 on Nov. 2 to put the municipal building at 1645 Art School Road, where the Chester Springs theater has worked for more than a decade, up for bid to help pay for a new municipal and police building on Kimberton Road that closes Nov. 13. SALT recently spent $400,000 on the space under a 10-year licensing deal, but the bid terms do not require a buyer to honor it.

title: Chester County keeps its Triple-A rating from all three agencies
summary: S&P Global, Fitch and Moody's each reaffirmed the county's top credit rating with a stable outlook, keeping it the only Pennsylvania county rated Triple-A across the board and in the top 2 percent of counties nationally. The agencies pointed to reserves above 10 percent of spending and conservative budgeting; the rating lowers borrowing costs on capital projects.
loc: Chester County Government Services Center, 601 Westtown Road, West Chester

title: Veterans supply drive turns nonprofit, celebrates with Dec. 11 concert at the History Center
summary: The Drumroll Please Project, started seven years ago by percussion teacher Anthony Cracchiolo to collect supplies for veterans at the Coatesville VA, is now a registered Pennsylvania charity and marks it with a launch party and benefit concert from 7:30 to 11 p.m. Friday, Dec. 11, at 225 N. High St. Tickets are $20 in advance or $30 at the door, toward a $15,000 goal for clothing, hygiene supplies, food and rideshare cards.
loc: Chester County History Center, 225 N. High St., West Chester

title: Turnpike opens six lanes through the Downingtown stretch after three years of work
summary: The $214 million rebuild between mileposts 312 and 316 replaced four lanes with three in each direction, 12-foot lanes, wider shoulders and median, three new mainline bridges and 28 stormwater basins. Work began in May 2023 and was paid for with toll revenue as part of the Turnpike's statewide total reconstruction program.

title: Malvern voters shrink Borough Council to five seats; East Whiteland grows its board
summary: In Tuesday's election Malvern residents approved cutting Borough Council from seven members to five, while next door East Whiteland voted 64 percent in favor of expanding its Board of Supervisors from three to five after a resident petition drive sparked by a 1.5 million-square-foot data center. Tredyffrin voters also approved updates to their home rule charter.
loc: Malvern Borough Hall, 1 E. First Ave., Malvern

title: Improv troupe turns audience ideas into a Nov. 14 fundraiser at Uptown
summary: Better Than Bacon Improv headlines Comedy for a Cause at Uptown Knauer Performing Arts Center on Saturday, Nov. 14 at 7:30 p.m., with musical comedian Todd Chappelle opening. Proceeds from the show, wine grab and silent auction go to the Coatesville Youth Initiative and Brandywine Valley Active Aging; tickets are $31 for members and $36 otherwise.

title: WCU stages the Pennsylvania premiere of Amy Beach's opera Cabildo Nov. 13-14
summary: West Chester University Opera Theatre performs the one-act Cabildo at 7:30 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 and 3 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14 in the Asplundh Concert Hall at 700 S. High St., with the lobby dressed as a 1930s New Orleans museum and performers greeting the audience in character. The show runs under an hour in English with supertitles; tickets are $8.25 and free for children 12 and under and WCU students, faculty and staff.
loc: Philips Memorial Building, 700 S. High St., West Chester

title: Hometown Christmas Parade returns Dec. 4 with more marching bands
summary: The Greater West Chester Chamber of Commerce's free parade runs Friday, Dec. 4, rain or shine, starting with the tree lighting at 6:30 p.m. and the procession at 7. This year's lineup adds marching bands by popular demand, works in an America250 tribute and ends with Santa.

title: Refill shop opens on East Street Road for soap, pasta and skincare by the ounce
summary: West Chester Refillery Station, which held its grand opening Oct. 24 at 54 E. Street Road near the new Goodwill, sells household and personal-care products in bulk: bring or buy a container, weigh it, fill it and pay only for the product. The husband-and-wife owners say many shoppers come in to buy just enough to try something.

title: History Center lights up for a monthlong Season of Lights starting Dec. 2
summary: The Chester County History Center fills its galleries with illuminated displays and decorated trees from Dec. 2 through Jan. 2, open Wednesday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., and closed Dec. 25 and Jan. 1. The exhibit is included with regular admission: $10 adults, $7 seniors, $5 children and students.
loc: Chester County History Center, 225 N. High St., West Chester
